axis: obviousness held against a thing → clarity counted to its credit

members.tone: The plain term for the property, stating that a thing reaches the mind without effort and passing no judgement on whether that is a merit.
Faintly disapproving - the obviousness is heard as something laid on too thickly, an excess where *unsubtle* reports only a lack.
Criticism by subtraction - it names the delicacy that is missing rather than the heaviness that replaced it, so the fault reads as a deficiency.
Approving of edges - the outline is sharp enough that there is no blurred margin left to argue over.
The cool member of its group - sharpness of definition reported as a fact, without the approval in *clear-cut* or the bite of *trenchant*.
Praise with an edge on it - the definition cuts rather than merely bounds, a force *distinct* never claims.
Praise for language that offers no resistance at all, clarity felt as smoothness rather than as precision.
Plainer praise than *limpid* - the clarity is credited to the ordering of the thought rather than to the ease of the surface.
Formal to the point of ornament - the compliment is paid in exactly the diction the clarity it commends would strip out.
Polished praise - the language is treated as something seen straight through, admired for the absence of anything between reader and sense.
The blunt, emphatic option - it insists nothing has been left to misread, with none of the polish of *pellucid*.
Formal and assessing - clarity approved as a property the language can be judged to have, not a pleasure it gives.
Neutral and provisional - it marks how a thing stands on first sight and reserves whatever a closer look might overturn.
Force without approval - it makes clarity a matter of no other reading being available, which serves the unwelcome as readily as the welcome.
Warm praise - the clarity comes with the freshness of something being undergone now, not merely well set out.
